subject: Ledger fingerprint & PO serial reconciliation for Lumenscale onboarding
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rana <priya.rana@lumenscale.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Ledger fingerprint and PO serial details (Lumenscale onboarding)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for starting the onboarding packet. We started a quick audit of the PO issuance flow and noticed a mismatch between the vendor's submitted line-item IDs and how our ledger fingerprinting is assigning PO serials. In a few cases the same vendor SKU is being split across multiple serials, which causes downstream billing and spend-cap enforcement to treat them as separate commitments.

Two asks to make the initial provisioning smooth:
- Can you share the vendor's preferred PO serial pattern (example prefix + sequence) or confirm if Lumenscale can accept a single master PO with sub-line items?
- Attached is our short onboarding form — it asks for accounting codes and the single-line vs multi-line preference (lumenscale_onboard_form.pdf). If you can return that, we can lock the serial mapping.

Tentative plan from our side: map any incoming PO serial to a single procurement token per vendor and normalize SKU lines during acceptance. That will require a one-time mapping file (po-matrix.csv) which we can share after your confirmation.

Appreciate a reply by end of week if possible — want to avoid a spend-cap misclassification on the first invoice.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Vendor Enablement Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Attachments: lumenscale_onboard_form.pdf (PDF, 72KB)
From: Priya Rana <priya.rana@lumenscale.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Duval <alex.duval@lumenscale.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ledger fingerprint and PO serial details (Lumenscale onboarding)

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the heads up. We saw the split on your intake as well when we submitted the initial CSV. Lumenscale uses a PO serial format of LUM-YYYY-##### by default, but we can accept a master PO number if Redwood prefers to consolidate. I attached our export of the PO matrix that shows the SKU mapping and current preferred serials (po-matrix.csv).

On spend caps: our procurement policy typically sets a 90-day rolling cap per vendor; for this engagement we can provision a temporary cap of $150,000 and adjust after go-live. If Redwood needs a hard cap enforced on your side, confirm the exact numeric limit and we will surface it on our side too.

I've filled out the onboarding form with accounting codes where possible — see the PDF return (attached). Let us know if anything looks missing.

Best,
Priya Rana
Senior Procurement Manager | Lumenscale
priya.rana@lumenscale.com
Attachments: po-matrix.csv (CSV, 18KB); filled_lumenscale_onboard_form.pdf (PDF, 86KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rana <priya.rana@lumenscale.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ledger fingerprint and PO serial details (Lumenscale onboarding)

Thanks Priya — that helps a lot.

Quick responses and proposed actions:
1) Serial pattern: we'll accept LUM-YYYY-##### as the vendor-provided format, but to avoid splits we'll canonicalize to a Redwood procurement token that references the vendor serial (internal mapping only). Example canonical token: RWD-LUM-20261125-001 which we will include in the memo field of the master PO.

2) Line-item normalization: Connor will run a one-time normalization job to merge fragmented SKU lines from your CSV into single logical lines on our ledger. That will preserve unit prices and quantities but present a single line for spend-cap enforcement.

3) Spend cap: agree to the temporary $150,000 cap. We will enforce this on issuance and emit an alert if new commitments approach 90% of that cap. If Lumenscale wants an absolute block, confirm and we'll flip to a hard cap.

4) Deliverables & timeline:
- Connor: receive the po-matrix.csv and a brief mapping spec by EOD tomorrow.
- Vanessa: prepare the master PO serialing format and the DocuSign envelope for our standard procurement terms.
- Priya: confirm whether you want hard cap enforcement.

On the mapping CSV: I looked at the sample and saw three rows with vendor_line_id mismatches (lines 12, 34, 57). Connor — can you reconcile those and send back the corrected matrix by Monday?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Procurement Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Priya / team —

Quick update from engineering/ops after reconciling the matrix: I ran the normalization pass and corrected the three mismatched rows Markus flagged. The canonical mapping now maps vendor serials to a single RWD token. Example output snippet:
- Vendor: LUM-20261115-003 -> RWD-LUM-20261125-001 (master PO)
- Vendor: LUM-20261115-003-ALT -> RWD-LUM-20261125-001 (merged)

I created the master PO in the system with the spend cap set to $150,000 (soft enforcement + alert at 135K). If Lumenscale wants a hard block we can change to hard enforcement but will need signed confirmation.

DocuSign for the master PO + TA (standard terms) is live here: https://docusign.net/s/abc123 — Priya, if you can sign the envelope I will finalize issuance and share the final po-mapping export.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Procurement Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
